proof_summary: A tail-sum transform turns the dynamics into an integer-averaging flow bounded by the staircase \(N-j\), and monotone deficit clearing shows that stabilization is exactly the first time the penultimate flow reaches \(1\). Comparing source sizes \(N\) and \(N+1\), their pointwise difference is Boolean and a unit propagates along the saturated staircase diagonal, forcing the new hit within two further steps, while the averaging recurrence keeps the new endpoint zero through the old hitting time; thus the new hitting time is strictly larger but at most two larger.
